input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes on us a three-year USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights." That is walk-away territory under MINCOMMIT and fails the fallback, which would allow a commitment only for the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty. It also conflicts with Section 9.4 (our convenience termination with refund of prepaid Fees), Section 7.1 (no unidentified minimum-use charge) and Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment). The minimal fix restores the preferred position: Fees only for Services ordered and actually provided, with no shortfall charge; a 12-month reducible commitment with true-up remains available as a fallback.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer has no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, or volume commitment. Customer shall pay Fees only for Services ordered under an Order Form and actually provided, and no shortfall or unused-commitment charge applies.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced it with fees for Services actually ordered and provided, consistent with Sections 7.1, 9.4 and 12.3. If Copperleaf needs a commitment, we can discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalized.
proposal.summary: Remove the three-year take-or-pay minimum and pay only for Services ordered and provided.
